description: Give one athlete a training philosophy written for them, rather than one of the six built-ins. Starts from a built-in named by based_on and overlays whatever is supplied, so a philosophy that is "polarised but with a weekly tempo" is two fields rather than eight. The three shares of distribution must add up to 100 because the planner does arithmetic with them, and the call is rejected with the reason when they do not. `limits` carries the numbers the audit checks a week against — how many quality days, how many easy ones, how far off the distribution may drift — so a rule for this athlete is enforced rather than merely described. Sets the athlete onto it in the same write — a philosophy stored without being selected has no effect. Moving them back off it is update_athlete with philosophy set to a built-in id, or to null for the app default. tripeak://guide/philosophies describes the six and what each is for.

athlete_id.description: May be omitted when you coach exactly one athlete.

based_on.description: The built-in this starts from: polarised, pyramidal, threshold, sweetspot, aerobic-base or reverse. Fields left out are taken from it, and it is named in the philosophy's evidence line so the provenance of the thing is not lost.

caution.description: Where it goes wrong. An honest one is worth more than a flattering one.

character.description: The archetype in a few words, e.g. "The Physiologist".

distribution.description: Roughly how a week's training time is spread, as percentages of total time summing to 100.

limits.description: The same intentions as principles, in numbers audit_plan and create_workouts check a week against. Left out, they are inherited from based_on. This is how "this athlete can only take two hard days" becomes a check rather than a sentence in a briefing nobody can test.

distributionTolerancePp.description: Percentage points a zone may sit off the target distribution before the week is called off-plan. Ten is about one session in a ten-hour week.

minEasyDaysPerWeek.description: Days a week with nothing quality on them.

qualityDaysPerWeek.description: Hard or long-moderate days a week this philosophy plans for.

principles.description: How this coach plans, in the imperative. This is the part that reaches the planner, so it carries the weight: "long ride every Saturday, aerobic throughout" plans something, "believes in consistency" does not.

tagline.description: One sentence: what it commits to.

name: set_training_philosophy
